text.p: Asarco Inc has repurchased 845,000 shares through July 30 at a price of $27 million under the $100 million repurchase program announced June 26, chief executive Richard Osborne said Friday.

He told the company's quarterly analysts' meeting the company expects to continue to be aggressive in repurchasing shares. At current prices, the remaining $73 million will enable Asarco to acquire an additional 2.1 million shares. When announced, he
told Reuters later, the $100 million would have reduced the number of shares outstanding at the current price by 8 percent.
At the stock's present price -- 33-11/16 at Friday's close -- the $100 million will reduce shares outstanding 7 percent to 40 million from 43 million shares, he added.

Osborne also told analysts the Silver Bell mine near Tucson, Arizona, began production on schedule in July as an SX/EW -- solvent extraction/electrowinning -- operation. Asarco holds a 75 percent interest in the Silver Bell venture with Mitsui & Co Ltd .

"The start up has been smooth, so far," he said, adding "We've started up on schedule and on budget." The operation has an annual capacity to produce 36 million pounds of copper cathode at an estimated cash cost of $0.50 per pound.

Noting Asarco's June 12th sale of 20 million Grupo Mexico SA L shares in a private placement to institutional investors outside the United States, Osborne said, the sale, at a price of 22 pesos per share, created a liquid market for the shares for the first time.
Noting the L shares' discount to the B shares has declined from 21 percent at the time of the sale, he said "I ultimately expect the L to trade at par, or a premium to the B shares."
The company made a second private placement of 20 million L shares, at a price of 24 pesos per share, it announced on June 26.
Osborne said Asarco continues to hold 61 million L shares and 58 million B shares with an approximate market value of $280 million, adding it will make "further sales when market conditions permit."
